items.title: GHS unveils new framework to improve Ghana’s preparedness for health emergencies
items.description: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) has launched a new Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) framework to strengthen Ghana’s preparedness and response to disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. The framework brings together institutions, information, expertise, and resources to enable a more coordinated response when emergencies occur. Speaking at the launch, GHS Director-General Professor Samuel Kaba Akoriyea said the PHEOC system would provide a platform for coordinated action without taking over the statutory responsibilities of other institutions. “Importantly, the PHEOC does not replace the statutory mandates of other institutions. Rather, it provides a platform through which their mandates, capabilities, information and resources can be brought together to support coordinated public health emergency action,” he said. Five strategic and operational documents were launched as part of the initiative. They are the National PHEOC Strategic Plan 2026–2030, National PHEOC Handbook 2026, National PHEOC Standard Operating Procedures, Volume One, National Health Workforce Surge Strategic Plan 2026, and National Public Health Workforce Surge Management Standard Operating Procedures, Volume Two. Professor Akoriyea said the framework would support Ghana’s implementation of the International Health Regulations 2005, address gaps identified through the Joint External Evaluation and strengthen the country’s broader health security agenda. The GHS Director-General said the experiences of the Ebola outbreak in West Africa and the COVID-19 pandemic had demonstrated the need for countries to build emergency preparedness before crises occur. He recalled the isolation of Liberia and Sierra Leone during the 2014 Ebola outbreak and the widespread disruption caused by COVID-19 several years later. “Barely five years later, in 2019 and 2020, you and I witnessed our world shut down, travel limitations with numerous lockdowns, economic activities reduced to a minimum,” he said. He said Ghana must draw lessons from those experiences to ensure that future emergencies do not overwhelm the country’s response systems. Professor Akoriyea cautioned that the effectiveness of the framework would ultimately depend on implementation rather than the documents themselves. “The launch of these documents is not an end in itself. It marks the beginning of the next and more important phase—the phase we call implementation,” he said. He called on stakeholders to ensure that emergency operations centres remain functional, connected and sustainable. “Our task now is to move from documents to action, from structures to functionality, and from preparedness on paper to readiness in practice,” he added. According to him, Ghana’s emergency response system must be capable of coordinating action before, during, and after a public health emergency. “Success is measured by our readiness to coordinate seamlessly when an emergency occurs,” he said. Professor Akoriyea also stressed the need for public health emergency preparedness to extend beyond the health sector. He called for stronger collaboration among government institutions, security and emergency services, academia, research institutions, civil society, the private sector and development partners. “Public health emergency preparedness and response cannot be the responsibility of the health sector alone. It requires connected leadership and strong multisectoral coordination, timely information sharing, clear accountability and collective action,” he said. The development of the framework involved the Ministry of Health, GHS, regional health directorates, other ministries, departments and agencies, security and emergency services, academia, professional bodies, civil society organisations and private-sector stakeholders. Development partners, including the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the World Health Organization, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, and the Korea International Cooperation Agency, also supported the process. Professor Akoriyea acknowledged that the newly launched documents would require continuous improvement as Ghana gains more experience in managing public health emergencies. “Every book has Edition 1, Edition 2, etc. And it means that there will be setbacks. It’s not going to be perfect, but we are creating the platform for the next generation to take over and develop Edition 2,” he said. He subsequently declared the national PHEOC documents officially launched and urged stakeholders to translate the framework into practical action. The GHS believes the initiative will strengthen Ghana’s ability to detect, coordinate and respond to future health emergencies while building a more resilient national health security system.

items.title: Électricité verte : l'Exécutif ouvre davantage le réseau aux producteurs privés
items.description: Le gouvernement met en consultation publique un projet de décret qui précise les conditions dans lesquelles les producteurs privés d’électricité verte pourront se raccorder aux réseaux de distribution et commercialiser leur production. Attendu par les opérateurs du secteur, le texte apporte plusieurs clarifications sur l’accès au réseau, les procédures de raccordement et les modalités de vente de l’électricité verte. Les règles d’accès des producteurs privés d’énergie renouvelable aux réseaux de distribution se précisent. Soumis à consultation publique par le ministère de la Transition énergétique et du Développement durable, un projet de décret fixe les modalités techniques et administratives applicables au raccordement des installations de production d’électricité verte ainsi qu’à la commercialisation de leur production. Le texte vise à mettre en œuvre les dispositions des articles 5 et 26 de la loi 13-09 relative aux énergies renouvelables, telle qu’elle a été modifiée et complétée. Il concerne plus particulièrement les installations de production d’électricité à partir de sources renouvelables raccordées aux réseaux de distribution moyenne tension. Au-delà de son caractère réglementaire, le projet apporte plusieurs précisions attendues par les investisseurs et les entreprises engagées dans des projets d’autoproduction ou de fourniture d’électricité verte. Il intervient alors que la demande pour une énergie décarbonée gagne en importance dans l’industrie marocaine, notamment parmi les entreprises tournées vers l’export. Un cadre détaillé pour le raccordement au réseau Le projet de décret définit les procédures que devront suivre les porteurs de projets souhaitant raccorder leurs installations aux réseaux de distribution. Les gestionnaires de réseaux seront appelés à examiner les demandes de raccordement sur la base d’études techniques portant notamment sur la capacité du réseau à accueillir de nouvelles unités de production, les contraintes techniques éventuelles ainsi que les coûts associés aux travaux nécessaires. Le texte encadre également les délais de traitement des demandes. Les distributeurs devront notamment produire un avis technique motivé portant sur la faisabilité du raccordement. Lorsque celui-ci s’avère impossible dans sa configuration initiale, des solutions alternatives pourront être proposées aux porteurs de projets. Le projet précise par ailleurs les modalités de réalisation des études de raccordement, les obligations des différentes parties ainsi que les conditions techniques devant être respectées pour l’injection de l’électricité produite dans le réseau. L’objectif affiché est de garantir à la fois la sécurité du système électrique et l’intégration de nouvelles capacités de production renouvelable dans des conditions transparentes et prévisibles. De nouveaux débouchés pour l’électricité renouvelable L’un des apports les plus significatifs du texte concerne les possibilités de commercialisation de l’électricité produite à partir de sources renouvelables. Le projet prévoit qu’un producteur raccordé au réseau national de transport ou aux réseaux de distribution puisse fournir de l’électricité à un ou plusieurs consommateurs raccordés au réseau, sous réserve des capacités disponibles. Le texte encadre également les conditions de calcul et de gestion des éventuels excédents d’électricité injectés dans le réseau. Il fixe les règles applicables aux échanges entre producteurs, distributeurs et consommateurs, ainsi qu’aux contrats de fourniture qui devront être conclus entre les différentes parties. Autre disposition notable : les gestionnaires des réseaux de distribution pourront acquérir jusqu’à 10 % du volume annuel total de l’électricité qu’ils distribuent auprès de producteurs d’énergie renouvelable. Cette électricité pourra être utilisée pour leurs propres besoins ou pour l’alimentation des consommateurs situés dans leur périmètre de desserte. Dans sa note de présentation, le ministère souligne que le texte devrait contribuer à faciliter l’intégration des énergies renouvelables dans le système électrique national, tout en offrant aux acteurs économiques de nouvelles possibilités d’approvisionnement en électricité verte. Une évolution qui répond à la montée des besoins en énergie décarbonée des secteurs industriels, agricoles et de services, de plus en plus soumis aux exigences environnementales des marchés internationaux. items.title: Gunmen kill 15 policemen in Niger
items.description: Armed men killed 15 police officers in southwest Niger, near the west African country’s border with Nigeria and Benin, local sources told AFP Saturday. Although those responsible have not yet been identified, Friday’s attack was just the latest in a region prone to jihadist violence carried out by groups linked to al-Qaeda or the Islamic State (IS) group. This latest attack targeted a gendarmerie station near Tessa, in the Dosso region, a former local elected official told AFP. It was carried out by unidentified armed men on motorbikes “who probably came from neighbouring Nigeria”, he added. A local official confirmed the toll of 15 dead to AFP, without elaborating. Videos posted to social media by locals appear to show burnt-out vehicles and shelters inside the gendarmes’ compound. The victims of the attack were buried Saturday at a cemetery in the city of Dosso. The authorities in Niger have so far made no statement on the attack. Niger, governed by a military junta for three years, has been plagued by jihadist violence and saw a spate of kidnappings of Westerners last year. Earlier this month, state media and local sources said hundreds of people had fled their homes in the region after a series of attacks in mid-July against their villages. The border zone became the site of fresh jihadist violence in 2025 as groups affiliated to al-Qaeda or IS moved into the territory, according to the ACLED conflict monitor. items.title: Beach Volleyball: Nigeria beat Morocco, qualify for Los Angeles 2028 Olympics
items.description: Nigeria’s women’s beach volleyball team has qualified for the Olympic Games for the first time after defeating Morocco 2-0 in the final of the 2026 CAVB Women’s Beach Volleyball Championship in Alexandria, Egypt, on Saturday. The victory secured Nigeria’s place at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles, United States, where the team will represent the country in the beach volleyball event. Nigeria dominated the final, winning the two sets 21-17 and 21-10 to claim the gold medal and secure the Olympic qualification. The team had earlier booked its place in the final after defeating Mozambique 2-0 in the semi-final. Nigeria won both sets 21-17. Reacting to the achievement, President of the Nigeria Volleyball Federation (NVBF), Musa Nimrod, congratulated the team and described the qualification as a milestone for the country. “I wish to congratulate Nigerians and thank God. This is the fourth time we are going into the finals; we finished in second place on three occasions,” Nimrod said. “God has done it for us on our fourth trial and given us victory. It is not the Nigeria Volleyball Federation’s success alone but the entire nation,” he added. items.title: Benue Police targets youths in fresh push against cultism, violence
items.description: …launches POCACOV office By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State Police Command has intensified its engagement with young people in the state, launching a fresh campaign against cultism, violence, drug abuse and other forms of criminality as part of activities marking the 2026 National Youth Day. The initiative was unveiled during a stakeholders’ youth dialogue organised by the Command, which brought together representatives of student unions, youth associations and other youth-focused organisations across the state. The engagement also featured the kick-start of the Office of the Police Campaign Against Cultism and Other Vices (POCACOV) in Benue, designed to deepen advocacy and sensitisation among young people. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, disclosed this in a statement issued on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Cletus Nwadiogbu. Aondongu said the dialogue provided an avenue for the Police and youths to openly discuss issues affecting their safety and wellbeing, as well as ways of strengthening their role in promoting peaceful communities. He said discussions focused on discouraging electoral thuggery, cultism, cyberbullying, drug and substance abuse, violence and other criminal activities that could exploit young people or undermine security in the state. The Commissioner of Police urged youths to reject violence and criminal associations, stressing that they remained critical partners in maintaining peace and security across Benue. Nwadiogbu also charged them to use social media and other digital platforms responsibly and channel their energy and talents towards productive activities that would contribute to the development of the state. According to him, the newly established POCACOV office would sustain regular engagements with schools, student unions, youth organisations and other stakeholders to promote peace, responsible citizenship and crime prevention. The Command further assured that it would continue to build partnerships with youth groups across the state, while appreciating participants at the dialogue for their contributions and commitment to promoting peaceful coexistence. items.title: AJK PM Rathore urges dialogue to resolve crisis, calls for end to ‘base camp’ mindset
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore on Saturday said the biggest challenge for the incoming government would be to deal with the situation caused by the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee’s (JAAC) movement, stressing that dialogue was the only way to resolve the crisis. Speaking to a group of journalists at Kashmir House, Rathore said the current situation in AJK could become “alarming” and expressed hope that it would be resolved after the formation of the new government. He added the PML-N would have a major responsibility in this regard. Referring to the JAAC’s demands, he said while the body had been seeking the right to ownership, Poonch had ultimately been deprived of the right to representation. “I had promised the action committee that four refugee seats would be abolished, but its leaders did not accept my advice,” he said. “Even eight seats could have been abolished, but they remained adamant. “Had the action committee even given a hint, I would certainly have gone to Rawalakot,” Rathore added. The AJK premier also endorsed PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s proposal to establish a truth and reconciliation commission, saying it could provide all stakeholders a way out of the crisis. The regional government on June 5 declared the JAAC a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act. The notification by AJK’s Home Department said the group was “engaged in terrorism” and acted in a manner “prejudicial to peace and security” of the state. It further stated that JAAC was involved in “creating anarchy in the state by intimidating public, promoting hatred and creating a sense of insecurity in society and public at large etc”. Following the ban, local authorities launched a crackdown against the organisation, arresting scores of its leaders and activists from different areas. PML-N ‘rushed’ into elections He also alleged that the PML-N’s AJK leadership had rushed into the regional elections in its haste to acquire power. “Our position was that peace should first be restored in the state and elections should be held afterwards, but the PML-N insisted on holding elections and forming the government at all costs,” Rathore said, adding that AJK was now facing multiple challenges as a result. On the election results, Rathore said the PPP’s position was that it had not been provided a level playing field and alleged that various tactics had been used to ensure the PML-N’s victory. He claimed that some constituencies where the PPP had initially won were subsequently turned into defeats. The central leadership of PPP and PML-N had held several meetings over election-related issues, and the PML-N had assured the PPP leadership that its complaints would be addressed, he added. Defending the recent elections in his constituency , LA-17, Rathore claimed that Haveli was the only area where no rigging had taken place. He also rejected allegations of government interference in the elections, saying the PPP government had not interfered in the electoral process. Rathore regretted that the elections in Haveli had been unnecessarily highlighted, adding that, in the context of the area’s electoral history, the 2026 polls had been “extremely peaceful”. He recalled the 2011 elections , which had been followed by nearly a month of tension in the area, during which several shops were burnt and other property was damaged. The 2016 polls had also witnessed casualties and unrest and the 2021 elections, too, had been marked by tension, Rathore said. Responding to allegations of rigging by his PML-N rival, Engineer Chaudhry Mohsin Aziz, Rathore said the PPP would respond to the allegations at every forum. “If any candidate has a complaint about rigging, constitutional and legal forums, including election tribunals, are available. They can approach these forums with evidence,” he said. “On what basis could Chaudhry Mohsin have defeated me?” He maintained that people in his constituency acknowledged his development work but attributed his electoral challenge to the small size of his clan. “In other words, even the people of my constituency admit that I carried out development work there,” he said, pointing to the approval of a Danish school, a university, several roads and a power project in Haveli. “I had already said that if I lost, I would quit politics.” Rathore also called for an overhaul of what he described as the region’s “obsolete” system of governance and urged people to move beyond the traditional notion of AJK being merely the “base camp” of the Kashmir freedom movement. “We should now move beyond the thinking that Azad Kashmir is the base camp of the freedom movement,” he said. “Only when there is construction and development can it truly become a base camp.” He deemed the existing system outdated and said it “could not continue any longer”, stressing the need to abandon traditional practices and focus on the region’s economic development, particularly through tourism and agriculture. “The AJK setup is already a model when there is talk in Pakistan about smaller provinces,” he explained. “We have to get out of traditional practices and work for the development of the region.” Polls are being held in three phases amid unrest in the region. So far, in the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N has secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party also joined hands with the PML-N, taking the alliance’s strength to 26. The PML-N on Wednesday announced its candidates for seven of the eight reserved seats in the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly. The special seats, for which elections have been scheduled for August 24, comprise five for women and one each for Ulema-i-Din or Mashaikh , Jammu and Kashmir state subjects residing abroad, and technocrats and other professionals.

items.title: Loroum/Cohésion sociale : Les forces vives de Banh s’engagent pour le vivre-ensemble et la cohésion sociale
items.description: BURKINA-LOROUM-DECENTRALISATION-CONCERTATION-COHESION Loroum/Cohésion sociale : Les forces vives de Banh s’engagent pour le vivre-ensemble et la cohésion sociale Ouahigouya, 21 août 2026 (AIB)-La délégation spéciale de Banh a tenu, ce vendredi 21 août 2026 à Ouahigouya, la première session de son cadre de concertation communale axée sur le bilan de la situation des Personnes déplacées internes (PDI) et le vivre-ensemble et la cohésion sociale. La première session ordinaire du cadre de concertation communal de Banh, délocalisé à Ouahigouya, tenue le vendredi 21 août 2026, a été marquée par les appels des autorités locales, coutumières et religieuses au renforcement de la cohésion sociale et du vivre-ensemble. Placée sous la présidence du secrétaire général de la province du Loroum, David Ayoro, représentant le Haut-commissaire, la session a réuni les autorités administratives, les chefs de services ainsi que les leaders coutumiers et religieux de la commune de Banh. Au-delà de l’évaluation de la situation des Personnes déplacées internes (PDI), les échanges ont porté sur les conditions nécessaires à une coexistence pacifique et durable entre les communautés d’accueil et les personnes déplacées. Pour le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Banh, Théophile Wendpouiré Zongo, la réussite de l’intégration repose notamment sur l’humilité, l’adaptation et le respect des règles établies au sein des communautés d’accueil. « Nous demandons aux personnes déplacées de faire preuve d’humilité, de s’adapter aux réalités de leurs communautés d’accueil et de respecter les règles qui y sont établies. Il faut donc se faire mutuellement confiance et veiller à respecter les dispositions sécuritaires mises en place », a-t-il déclaré. Le PDS a également appelé les populations hôtes à préserver leur élan de solidarité et à considérer les personnes déplacées comme des membres à part entière de leurs communautés. Abondant dans le même sens, le chef coutumier de Banh, l'Emir Moussa Alceny Barry, a salué la résilience et l’esprit de solidarité dont font preuve les populations face aux différentes épreuves traversées. « Je suis fier de mes populations qui ont démontré leur capacité à accueillir et à vivre en harmonie avec des personnes qu’elles ne connaissaient pas auparavant. Cette expérience témoigne d’une véritable solidarité et d’une bonne intégration », s'est-t-il réjoui. « Il les a encouragés à poursuivre cet effort de résilience, à renforcer le dialogue et à multiplier les échanges afin de consolider la cohésion sociale et le vivre-ensemble. A l’issue des travaux, les participants ont formulé entre autres des recommandations visant à renforcer l’intégration des PDI et à préserver les liens entre communautés. Agence d’information du Burkina DB/HB/OO

items.title: Suspected robber crashes stolen taxi into traders while fleeing mob at Ejisu
items.description: A suspected armed robber crashed a taxi he had allegedly attempted to steal after ramming it into some shops while trying to escape a mob at the Ejisu traffic junction. According to a witness, the suspect got into the car, a Toyota Corolla with registration number GT 1557-16, and attacked the driver, demanding he hand over the vehicle. As he tried to get away, a group of men surrounded the car and tried to pull him out, but he reversed sharply, ploughing into the shops nearby before crashing the vehicle. He managed to flee on foot, taking refuge inside a mobile money container as members of the public gave chase. Police officers arrived at the scene in time and rescued the suspect from the mob before he could sustain further harm. He has since been taken into custody. There have been no reports of injuries or casualties from the crash so far, and investigations into the incident are ongoing.

items.title: Faitière des communes du Togo : Les travaux de la commission “plaidoyer, coopération décentralisée et transfrontalière” lancés
items.description: Lomé, 21 août (ATOP) – La Faîtière des communes du Togo (FCT) a lancé, les travaux de la Commission plaidoyer, coopération décentralisée et transfrontalière, le vendredi 21 août à Lomé. Le lancement de cette commission s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet ” Coopération dans le domaine de la gouvernance territoriale au Togo (PAGT), financé par l’ambassade de France. Elle fait suite aux conclusions de l’Assemblée générale élective de la FCT du 5 mars 2026, tenue à Kara, créant des commissions dont celle dénommée Commission plaidoyer, coopération décentralisée et transfrontalière. Cette commission est un cadre de réflexions et d’analyse sur la thématique de la coopération décentralisée entre les communes togolaises et celles du reste du monde. Elle est chargée de formuler des recommandations sur la thématique aux organes dirigeants de la FCT. Composée de 22 maires, elle est présidée par le maire de la commune Lacs 1, Me Coffi Alexis Aquereburu. Le lancement de la commission a été couplée de sa première réunion qui a permis d’éclairer les participants sur l’organisation et le fonctionnement de la commission. Les membres ont élaboré une feuille de route des actions à mener, identifié les goulots d’étranglement qui freinent la coopération entre les communes et recueilli des propositions et de recommandations. La présidente de la FCT, Touni Koubonou a fait savoir que la commission a été créé pour relever des défis de l’insuffisance de gestion structurée, de déficit de communication, de méconnaissance des partenaires potentiels et de difficultés à mobiliser des ressources autour de projets. Elle a exprimé sa gratitude au Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, à l’Ambassade de France au Togo. Selon le président de la commission, la coopération décentralisée constitue un véritable levier de développement. « Elle offre à nos communes des possibilités de partage d’expériences, de renforcement des compétences, de mobilisation de ressources et, surtout, de construction de réponses concrètes aux besoins des populations » a-t-il expliqué. Me Aquereburu a souligné que la commission ne devrait pas être une structure supplémentaire qui se limiterait à formuler des recommandations, mais plutôt un véritable espace de réflexions, de dialogue et surtout d’actions, capable de faire remonter les réalités du terrain et de proposer à la FCT des solutions concrètes, réalistes et applicables. ATOP/EAG/MD

items.title: Kourittenga : La délégation spéciale de Pouytenga adopte plusieurs délibérations pour renforcer le développement communal
items.description: BURKINA-KOURITTENGA-COMMUNE-SESSION-DELIBERATION Kourittenga : La délégation spéciale de Pouytenga adopte plusieurs délibérations pour renforcer le développement communal Pouytenga, 22 août 2026 (AIB)- La troisième session extraordinaire de l’année 2026 de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Pouytenga s’est tenue du vendredi 21 au samedi 22 août 2026, sous la présidence du Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de ladite commune, Bénoit Tiemtoré. Plusieurs dossiers relatifs aux ressources humaines, aux partenariats, aux infrastructures, au développement économique local et à la gestion budgétaire ont été examinés et adoptés au cours de la session. Durant les deux jours de travaux, les membres de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Pouytenga ont d’abord procédé à la lecture et à l’amendement du procès-verbal de la deuxième session ordinaire, tenue du 11 au 12 juin 2026. Les échanges ont ensuite porté sur plusieurs délibérations relatives au renforcement des capacités de l’administration communale. A cet effet, la délégation spéciale a autorisé le recrutement, sur concours professionnel, de plusieurs agents au profit de la commune. Il s’agit notamment d’un administrateur civil, d’un attaché administratif, d’un assistant des services financiers, d’un assistant en gestion des ressources humaines et d’un adjoint administratif. Selon le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Pouytenga, Bénoit Tiemtoré, ces recrutements devraient contribuer à renforcer les capacités de l’administration communale et à améliorer la qualité des services offerts aux populations. « Nous avons un besoin crucial d’agents. Le personnel est insuffisant pour faire fonctionner les services et les animer comme il se doit afin de répondre aux besoins de la population. C’est pour cela que nous avons pris attache avec le Programme national de volontariat au Burkina Faso, qui nous accompagne », a-t-il ajouté. Pour le PDS, cela a nécessité la prise d’une délibération pour autoriser la signature d’une convention avec ce programme, pour une durée de trois ans, renouvelable si le besoin se fait sentir. La session a également accordé une place importante aux partenariats destinés à accompagner la commune dans la mise en œuvre de ses actions de développement. Ainsi, la délégation spéciale a autorisé la signature d’une convention avec l’Agence nationale d’appui au développement des collectivités territoriales (ADCT), dans le cadre de l’offre de 140 bourses destinées aux collectivités territoriales pour l’édition 2026-2028. Cette convention porte notamment sur le recrutement, la formation et la prise en charge des salaires d’agents devant contribuer au fonctionnement des collectivités bénéficiaires. Une autre délibération autorise la signature d’une convention entre le Groupement d’intérêt public – Programme national de volontariat au Burkina Faso (GIP-PNVB) et la commune de Pouytenga pour la mise à disposition de volontaires nationaux. Pour les membres de la délégation spéciale, ces différentes initiatives devraient contribuer à améliorer les services de proximité et à répondre davantage aux besoins des populations. « Je trouve que les délibérations prises dans ce cadre permettront de développer la commune. Nous, membres de la Délégation spéciale, avons à cœur les préoccupations de la population. Les décisions que nous prenons visent à favoriser son épanouissement. Il y aura une amélioration de la main-d’œuvre au niveau des services. Il y a d’autres attentes, mais avec le temps, tout ira bien », a déclaré le Kol Naaba de Pouytenga. Sur le volet des infrastructures, les membres ont examiné et autorisé la signature d’un avenant dans le cadre de l’aménagement de la cité du 11-Décembre 2019. Ils ont également adopté une délibération portant réaménagement du budget annexe de ladite cité. La question du développement économique local a également été inscrite à l’ordre du jour. A ce titre, ils ont autorisé l’adhésion de la commune au processus d’élaboration et de mise en œuvre de la Stratégie de développement économique local et de cohérence territoriale (S-DELCoT). Enfin, la délégation spéciale a examiné une délibération portant réaménagement du budget rectificatif n°1, gestion 2026. Agence d’information du Burkina WMGN/AWS/HB/OO

items.title: Droits de douane : le PM canadien promet une riposte équivalente aux nouvelles mesures américaines
items.description: Le Canada ripostera aux nouvelles surtaxes américaines en imposant aux États-Unis des droits de douane d’un montant équivalent, a annoncé samedi le Premier ministre Mark Carney. « Le Canada appliquera des droits de douane équivalents, au dollar près, afin de protéger nos travailleurs et nos entreprises », a déclaré M. Carney dans un communiqué. Cette décision intervient alors que les négociations commerciales entre Ottawa et Washington ont échoué à aboutir à un accord permettant d’éviter l’entrée en vigueur de nouvelles taxes américaines sur plusieurs produits canadiens. « Les changements de dernière minute apportés par les États-Unis étaient injustes, irrationnels sur le plan économique et remettaient en question la fiabilité de tout accord », a estimé Mark Carney, annonçant la suspension des négociations commerciales avec Washington. Le Premier ministre canadien a également reconnu que la relation entre les deux pays avait profondément changé depuis le début de la guerre commerciale. Le président américain Donald Trump avait annoncé ces nouveaux droits de douane en juillet. Leur entrée en vigueur, initialement prévue mercredi, avait été repoussée de trois jours. Les États-Unis demeurent le principal partenaire commercial du Canada. Environ 70 % des exportations canadiennes sont actuellement destinées au marché américain. items.title: Kompienga/Santé : La campagne chimio prévention paludisme saisonnier se poursuit avec le porte-à-porte pour protéger les enfants
items.description: KOMPIENGA-PAMA-SANTE- CAMPAGNE CPS Kompienga/Santé : La campagne chimio prévention paludisme saisonnier se poursuit avec le porte-à-porte pour protéger les enfants Pama, 21 août 2026 (AIB)-Dans le cadre de la campagne chimio prévention contre le paludisme saisonnier (CPS) 2026 phase 2, le district sanitaire de Pama est en plein campagne contre le paludisme dans les villes de Pama et Kompienga avec la stratégie de porte-à-porte pour protéger les enfants de 3 à 59 mois. Prévue du 20 au 23 août 2026, la campagne chimio prévention contre le paludisme saisonnier cible les enfants de 3 à 59 mois et consiste à administrer un traitement antipaludique préventif et aussi un dépistage de la malnutrition aiguë auprès de cette catégorie. Pour les infirmiers et les Agents de santé à base communautaire (ASBC), la campagne se déroule dans de bonnes conditions. « Grâce à la stratégie du porte-à-porte, aucun enfant ne devrait être laissé de côté », ont-ils indiqué. Ils ont invité par ailleurs les parents à s'impliquer dans la prise de ces médicaments dont l'efficacité dans la prévention contre le paludisme n'est plus à démontrer. Cependant, certaines exceptions sont à prendre en compte. Il s’agit notamment des enfants ciblés mais malades ou présentant de la fièvre, de ceux déjà sous traitement antipaludique, des enfants allergiques à la SP-AQ, ainsi que de ceux ayant pris du cotrimoxazole au cours des 28 derniers jours, ne sont pas concernés par la campagne. Agence d’information du Burkina HO/HB/OO

items.title: Reject thuggery, IGP Disu tasks Nigerian youths
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has challenged Nigerian youths to reject political and digital thuggery and use their energy, talents and influence to promote peace, responsible citizenship and national development. Disu gave the charge at the closing ceremony of the International Youth Day 2026 National Youth Leadership and Security Initiative of the Nigeria Police Force, held under the theme, “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations,” with the campaign slogan, “My Future Is Greater Than Political and Digital Thuggery.” The IGP said the three-day initiative provided an opportunity to engage young Nigerians, examine the country’s security realities and strengthen the role of youths in building a peaceful and prosperous Nigeria. He said activities including panel discussions, a walkathon and tree-planting exercise demonstrated that youth engagement must go beyond speeches to create understanding, responsibility and concrete action. According to him, although Nigerian youths may come from different backgrounds, speak different languages and hold divergent opinions, they share common aspirations for peace, security, opportunity and dignity. Disu warned youths against allowing themselves to be used as instruments of political violence, particularly ahead of the 2027 general elections. “This initiative must not end when the chairs are cleared,” the IGP said, stressing that the Police campaign, “My Future Is Greater Than Political and Digital Thuggery,” was designed to encourage young Nigerians to protect their future from manipulation. He urged youths not to allow anyone to use their present circumstances to destroy their future, saying they have a critical role to play in ensuring peaceful democratic participation. The IGP also highlighted the importance of recognising positive youth leadership, noting that the Youth Honours and Awards introduced during the initiative were intended to celebrate young Nigerians making meaningful contributions to society. He charged the award recipients to see the recognition as a responsibility to continue leading, innovating and serving their communities while creating opportunities for others. Disu further announced the formal recognition of Youth Ambassadors Ann Nwawhodoh and Olugbenga “GB” Agboola, who will serve as a bridge between the Nigeria Police Force and Nigerian youths. He urged the ambassadors to listen to young people, understand their realities and help build a stronger relationship between the Police and the youth population. According to him, effective security cannot be achieved by the Police alone, stressing that security is a shared responsibility requiring collaboration between law enforcement agencies and citizens. The IGP described the Abuja Youth Declaration on Peace, Responsible Citizenship and Democratic Participation as one of the most significant outcomes of the three-day initiative. He urged participants to transform the declaration from a document into a living commitment by choosing peace over violence, dialogue over conflict, truth over misinformation and nation-building over destruction. “Own this Declaration. Take it to your schools, your communities, your organisations and your digital spaces. And live by it,” Disu told the youths. He challenged young Nigerians to recognise themselves as part of the solution to the country’s challenges, warning that their generation could either be manipulated into destroying communities or become the generation that builds them. The choice is yours. And history will judge your generation not by what you inherited, but by what you did with it,” he said. The IGP commended development and international partners, civil society organisations, government institutions, private-sector sponsors, facilitators, speakers, volunteers and the organising committee for their contributions to the initiative. He also praised officers and personnel of the Nigeria Police Force who worked to make the programme successful, while appreciating the young participants for their openness and enthusiasm. Disu assured that the Police would take the initiative beyond Abuja to schools, tertiary institutions, NYS formations and youth organisations across the country. He said the Force would continue to promote preventive policing, responsible digital citizenship, peaceful democratic participation and stronger Police-youth partnerships. The IGP urged Nigerian youths to carry the message of the initiative into their communities, schools, homes and digital spaces, reminding them that every great change begins with an individual choice. “My future is greater than political and digital thuggery. Let us choose peace, responsibility and Nigeria,” he declared. Disu thereafter formally declared the International Youth Day 2026 National Youth Leadership and Security Initiative of the Nigeria Police Force closed, with a call for Nigerian youths to become active partners in building a safer and more prosperous country. items.title: Okonkwo’s Charlton deliver blow to Hammers with London derby triumph
items.description: Charlton maintained their perfect start to the Championship season with a 2-1 victory at West Ham on Saturday that added to the pressure on Hammers boss Nuno Espirito Santo. Lloyd Jones and Tyreece Campbell Charlton 2-0 up in the London derby before Joel Piroe, on loan from Leeds, pulled one back on his West Ham debut. Taty Castellanos missed a stoppage-time penalty for the Hammers, relegated from the Premier League last season, as Charlton made it two wins from two. Southampton bounced back from defeat by Watford as Divin Mubama scored a dramatic late goal on his home debut to help the Saints secure a 3-1 victory over former club Stoke. Almost a year ago, the Manchester City loan striker was sent off for Stoke at St Mary’s for diving. Ryan Manning scored an injury-time penalty after Svante Ingelsson was sent off for bringing down Samuel Edozie. Cyle Larin bagged his third goal in as many games to give Tonda Eckert’s side an early lead but Stoke hit back through Ethan Galbraith. Southampton have been deducted four points and were expelled from the Championship play-off final after being found guilty of spying on a training session of Middlesbrough, the side they beat in the semi-final in contravention of league rules. Fer Lopez scored two goals as Wolves secured their first win of the season with a 3-1 success away to Preston. Blackburn stunned Middlesbrough with two goals in six second-half minutes to earn a 2-1 victory at Ewood Park, while Wrexham drew 1-1 with Watford in front of Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney. Cardiff remain unbeaten two games into their return to the second tier after Cian Ashford and Yousef Salech’s goals secured a 2-2 draw at Derby. Tairyk Arconte scored his first two goals for Millwall as they overwhelmed 10-man Norwich 3-0 to earn their second successive win. Norwich, who’ve now lost both of their opening games, had defender Jose Cordoba sent off in the second half at The Den. Portsmouth claimed their first win of the campaign with a 3-1 success at Lincoln. Demarai Gray rescued a point for Birmingham with a late penalty in a 2-2 draw at home to Bristol City. QPR drew 0-0 with Bolton at Loftus Road and it was a similar story for Sheffield United, under threat of a 12-point deduction for unpaid debts, as they played out their second goalless stalemate of the season at Swansea. items.title: Oil industry veteran Bosun Olabiyi-Agoro emerges PENGASSAN president
items.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Members of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, PENGASSAN, have ushered in a new era with the election of Bosun Olabiyi-Agoro as its elected National President. He took over from Festus Osifo, who is the President of the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC. Olabiyi-Agoro emerged unopposed at the association’s first Quadrennial Delegates Conference held in Abuja on Saturday. A distinguished Petroleum Engineer, labour leader and industrial relations strategist, Olabiyi-Agoro brings more than two decades of experience in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry to the leadership of the influential workers’ association. He currently serves with the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, NUPRC. Before joining the regulatory commission, he built an extensive technical and operational career with leading industry players, including Baker Hughes and EA Temile and Sons. His professional background is complemented by strong academic credentials. The President holds a Master’s degree in Petroleum Engineering from the University of Aberdeen, United Kingdom; a Post Graduate Certificate in Computing from London Metropolitan University, United Kingdom; and a Bachelor of Technology degree in Chemical Engineering from Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Ogbomoso. He is also an alumnus of Government College Ibadan. Olabiyi-Agoro is no stranger to organised labour and trade union leadership. He is the current Chairman of the Trade Union Congress, TUC, Oyo State Council, and has held several key positions within PENGASSAN. His previous positions include National Financial Secretary of PENGASSAN between 2022 and 2023, National Auditor from 2020 to 2022, and Chairman of the Baker Hughes PENGASSAN Branch from 2016 to 2020. Over the years, the new PENGASSAN president has participated in several local and international training programmes covering leadership, negotiation and industrial relations. He is widely regarded within labour circles for his clarity of purpose, straightforward approach and commitment to workers’ welfare. His emergence is expected to bring his blend of technical expertise, industry experience and trade union leadership to the forefront as PENGASSAN begins a new chapter under his stewardship. In his acceptance speech, the new president promised, among others, to prioritise workers’ welfare and continue with the legacies set by Osifo. items.title: Govt blames PTI for 'violating' SC order, says family committed contempt by issuing statements
items.description: The government on Saturday blamed the PTI for “violating” a Supreme Court (SC) order by issuing statements and speaking to the media following former prime minister Imran Khan’s medical check-up at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) on Friday. “PML-N believes that health issues should not be used for political gain,” Information Minister Attaullah Tarar told the media. He added that, whether in opposition or in government, the PML-N’s stance had always remained the same: politics and health issues should not be linked. The minister also accused Imran of issuing statements and releasing videos about the health of PML-N leaders when they were incarcerated and he was prime minister. Tarar added that since the SC order regarding Imran’s health was issued, “our government has not mocked him or made any controversial statements”. Recounting events of the past few days, Tarar said that after the SC order was issued, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar had explained the government’s position on it in detail. “The viewpoint was that whatever will happen, it will be according to the law,” Tarar said. He added that the government’s review petition “respectfully questioned whether the facility was available to every prisoner”. Secondly, he said, the petition questioned whether the law and Constitution allowed Imran to be examined at a private hospital. Tarar then elaborated on the implementation of the SC’s order. “The next question is whether the order was implemented. The answer is yes. Was the check-up conducted? Yes. Was it done transparently? Yes. Was his sister present? Yes. Were doctors from Shifa [Hospital] present? Yes. All the obligations were fulfilled.” Tarar also addressed the communication of these developments to the media and the general public. He said that shortly after the government filed its review petition, the law minister had explained its grounds in detail. He added that after Imran’s check-up was completed at Pims, he himself posted an update on X. Tarar said he was “surprised” by the PTI’s subsequent statements and actions. “PTI is miles away from the light of knowledge,” he said, adding that the party would not have filed a contempt petition had it been aware of the situation. “A baseless contempt petition has been filed .” The facts were shared with the public immediately, he said, adding that the government had maintained transparency throughout. “Contempt has definitely happened,” he said, adding that the SC had directed that no political motives should be involved in the medical check-up. However, Tarar said, people gathered outside Shifa Hospital, created social media content and removed barriers. “Wasn’t it the PTI that did this? Didn’t they violate the court order?” He added that the PTI had also issued statements and spoken at press conferences. “If somebody is in contempt, it is Imran Khan’s sister and his party. “The prisoner’s family was in contempt. His party was in contempt by gathering people and creating problems for the authorities.” He remarked that this was the first time a political party had created problems for its own founder’s health and treatment. Tarar added that earlier the Pakistan Bar Council and Punjab Bar Council had issued statements saying that some lawyers associated with the two bodies were, in their personal capacities, issuing statements to politicise the matter. Both councils had clarified that the bar councils should be kept separate from the issue, he said. “Some lawyers have tried to pollute bar politics,” Tarar said. Eight members of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) on Saturday strongly condemned the government’s “blatant, wilful and deliberate violation” of the SC’s Aug 18 order. “The order of the SC was clear, unequivocal and binding yet the executive has chosen to disregard it and has acted in direct defiance of the court’s directions and violated the same,” said a statement issued by the members. Meanwhile, Vice Chairman of the PBC Pir Muhammad Masood Chistie clarified that the statement represented the views of those individual members and could not be treated as the collective position of the PBC. “You obstructed his path. You created a security situation there,” the minister said, addressing PTI leadership. He added that the medical report from Pims had stated that Imran was in good health, prompting the question: “Which illness are you doing politics on?” Imran’s medical treatment had never been stopped or paused and would continue as needed, the information asserted, urging PTI leaders and Imran’s family not to politicise legal or health matters, adding that they had “been in contempt” by commenting on the issue. Tarar issued the statement hours after Dr Uzma Khan, Imran’s sister, approached the SC seeking to initiate contempt proceedings against those responsible for violating its Aug 18 order to shift the incarcerated former premier to a private hospital in the federal capital. On Tuesday, the SC had ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board. The court had also ordered that Dr Uzma Khan and Dr Faisal Sultan — Imran’s personal physician — be present during the medical examination by the board. At the same time, Imran’s family members, PTI members and lawyers associated with him were barred from disclosing his health condition or medical reports to the media or the public until the next hearing. The next day, the government had filed a review plea against the court’s order to shift Imran to the private hospital, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice. However, the SC had returned the plea on Thursday with the objection that the contents of the affidavit and facts, along with the review petition filed under Article 188 of the Constitution, had not been properly drawn up and that one of the paper books of was not in order. The same night, elaborate arrangements were put in place in and around Shifa International Hospital, and all signs pointed to the PTI founder being brought there, in compliance with SC order. However, it became clear on Friday morning that Imran had been taken to Pims for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison. Meanwhile, the government on Thursday filed a fresh review petition against the SC’s Aug 18 order. The Islamabad chief commissioner again filed the plea, saying that his office had a direct, substantial and legally protected interest in the matter and that the Aug 18 order adversely affected its constitutional authority.

items.title: Canada-US rift deepens as Carney vows retaliatory tariffs after trade talks fail
items.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Saturday he would slap retaliatory tariffs on the United States after walking away from a “bad deal” on trade, deepening the rift between the longtime allies. Negotiations between the neighboring countries broke down on Friday in Washington, allowing new 50-per cent US tariffs impacting some $20 billion worth of goods, or 5.5pc of Canadian exports to the United States, to come into force. Impacted products range from hockey sticks to cement. US President Donald Trump had said Washington “should be able to have a deal with Canada”, citing his “good relationship” with Carney. But on Saturday, the Canadian prime minister said Trump had set conditions that were ultimately unacceptable. “We believed earlier this week that we were moving towards a mutually beneficial agreement,” Carney said in the Canadian capital, Ottawa. “In recent days, the United States proposed new terms that were uneconomic, unfair, and undermined the net benefits for Canada, and called into question the reliability of any deal. In short, they asked too much and they offered too little,” he said. “We cannot accept what they’ve offered, and we will not give what they’ve asked,” Carney said, accusing Trump of launching a trade “war”. “You’re at war when you get attacked. We got attacked,” Carney said. New Canadian tariffs will notably target the US steel and dairy industries and take effect on September 8. Carney said further details would come next week. On Friday, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Washington had offered “significant tariff reductions on steel, aluminum, autos and lumber” in exchange for concessions from Canada. A senior US official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, characterised the talks as candid and not acrimonious. Then in a Saturday interview with Fox News , Greer said the United States was “moving forward with measures that respond to Canadian retaliation.” Greer also noted it was not clear if trade talks could get back on track soon, saying, “we don’t have new talks planned with the Canadians.” ‘Significant pressure’ Canada has been seeking relief from Trump’s tariffs on autos, steel and aluminum, which have battered the country’s economy, forced job losses and strained what was once an iron-clad trade relationship. Canadian negotiators had been camped out in Washington this week to firm up a deal that aimed to address various flashpoints. The White House had alleged “discriminatory treatment” by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products in introducing the duties. They were originally set to take effect on Wednesday, before Trump issued a last-minute delay of three days, citing major progress in talks. Ryan Majerus, a former US commerce official who is now a trade lawyer with King and Spalding, told AFP that “both sides will face significant pressure in the coming days to find an off-ramp.” Senator Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota, a US state which borders Canada, warned that the escalating trade war will raise costs for her state’s small businesses, farmers and families. “Canada is Minnesota’s number 1 trading partner,” the Democratic lawmaker posted on X. “Minnesotans are paying for Trump’s chaos.” Beyond the latest tariffs, the United States and Canada still have to agree on revisions to the North American free trade agreement, USMCA, which Trump declined to renew in its current form. Bilateral ties have also been hurt by Trump’s repeated threats to make Canada the 51st US state . Trump was irked by Carney’s widely-touted January speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland in which the prime minister declared that the global order was experiencing a “rupture.” Carney has repeatedly said relations with the United States have been forever altered, and that Canada must reduce its reliance on its southern neighbor, which currently accounts for roughly 70pc of Canadian exports. “We’ve been under no illusions. We recognized from the start that America has changed,” Carney told reporters on Saturday. “We recognize that sometimes, its signature was written in pencil.”

items.title: Noureddine Melikechi : « J’ai trouvé une ressemblance entre le Tassili N’Ajjer et Mars »
items.description: Le chercheur algérien installé aux États-Unis, Noureddine Melikechi , est revenu sur son initiative de donner les noms de trois célèbres parcs algériens à des régions de la planète Mars. « Je fais partie d’une équipe scientifique qui travaille sur la planète Mars. Le premier projet, c’était Curiosity et le deuxième, Perseverance. Mais j’ai surtout travaillé sur Curiosity. Quand j’ai commencé à travailler et à apprendre de mes collègues, j’ai trouvé une ressemblance pertinente entre le Tassili N’Ajjer en particulier et certaines régions de la planète Mars », a expliqué le célèbre chercheur algérien à la NASA dans un entretien à RFI , diffusé vendredi 21 août. Cette ressemblance l’a interpellé et il s’est dit « pourquoi ne pas donner des noms de parcs algériens à des parties de la planète Rouge ? » et ses collègues scientifiques ont voté en faveur de cette proposition. Noureddine Melikechi a porté son choix sur le Tassili N’Ajjer dans le Sahara, le Djurdjura en Kabylie et le Ghoufi dans les Aurès. « C’était aussi pour rendre hommage au pays qui m’a formé et à ces parcs naturels, mais aussi surtout pour attirer l’attention sur les parcs naturels qui existent en Algérie et partout dans le monde pour les protéger. C’est un trésor universel qu'on devrait protéger et garder pour les générations futures », soutient-il. Recherche scientifique aux États-Unis : le constat de Melikechi Melikechi s’est exprimé aussi sur l’offensive de l’administration de Donald Trump contre les milieux scientifiques et universitaires, ainsi que sur la menace de cette politique sur l’avenir de la science dans le pays de l'Oncle Sam. Invité vendredi 21 août sur RFI , le chercheur algérien à la NASA, qui fait partie du programme martien de l’agence américaine, a expliqué comment les scientifiques vivent les coupes budgétaires imposées par l’administration américaine sur la recherche scientifique. Noureddine Melikechi : les chercheurs étrangers sont « un peu l'oxygène de la recherche aux États-Unis » « Au début, ça a été très compliqué », dit-il, précisant qu’il ne s’agit pas seulement de coupes budgétaires, car cela concerne aussi la question des visas pour les étudiants étrangers. « Comme vous le savez, 50 % des chercheurs dans les sciences, l'ingénierie, l'informatique sont nés à l'étranger », souligne le doyen du Kennedy College of Sciences de l'université du Massachusetts à Lowell. Pour lui, les chercheurs étrangers sont « un peu l'oxygène de la recherche aux États-Unis. Et quand on coupe cet oxygène, la recherche prend un coup ». Il trouve que l’offensive menée par Trump « n’a aucun sens », car c’est justement la recherche scientifique qui a fait la force des États-Unis. Toutefois, le chercheur algérien affirme que depuis deux ans environ, des universitaires se sont dressés contre cette politique et les coupes budgétaires, « et on voit que ça commence petit à petit à se corriger un peu ». Melikechi trouve que la politique « America First » de Donald Trump met effectivement en danger la coopération scientifique internationale des universités et centres de recherche américains. « Il ne faut pas qu’il y ait de frontière dans la science » « La science est universelle, il faut qu'on le comprenne. Il ne faut pas qu’il y ait de frontière, car c'est ce qui fait la force de l'humanité. On peut utiliser la science pour des choses très bonnes, comme découvrir des traitements contre les maladies… », a encore déclaré le scientifique algérien. De son point de vue, quel que soit le pays, « la science est universelle. On gagnerait tous à ce que les scientifiques travaillent ensemble », insiste-t-il, regrettant l’existence d’un recul dans ce domaine aux États-Unis. « Mais en même temps, il y a une force de résistance à ce mouvement ». Concernant la concurrence féroce menée actuellement par la Chine dans le domaine de la recherche, le chercheur algérien indique qu’on ne peut pas dire que tout est noir aux États-Unis. Mais il trouve que le « progrès immense en Chine est plutôt positif ». « Je trouve très positif que des pays investissent dans la science. Actuellement, 30 à 31 % des publications dans les revues les plus spécialisées viennent de Chine, alors que ce n'était pas le cas il y a quelques années », ajoute-t-il. Selon lui, cela montre qu'il y a un effort considérable qui fait que la Chine vient petit à petit côtoyer les États-Unis en tête du classement des pays qui investissent dans la recherche et dans les sciences. L’article Noureddine Melikechi : « J'ai trouvé une ressemblance entre le Tassili N'Ajjer et Mars » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Republic Bank-JoyNews Habitat Fair: Day 2 ends on high note as patrons enjoy exciting discounts
items.description: The second day of the Republic Bank-JoyNews Habitat Fair ended on a high at the Achimota Retail Centre, with a steady stream of patrons turning up to explore opportunities in housing, construction and home ownership. Despite intermittent drizzle in Accra, the weather did little to dampen the atmosphere as prospective homeowners, builders, industry professionals and other visitors moved around the fairgrounds, engaging exhibitors and exploring products and services tailored to their housing needs. From building materials and home financing to furnishing and construction solutions, exhibitors used the second day to showcase their offerings, answer questions and guide visitors through the options available to them. For many patrons, the fair provided more than just an opportunity to browse products. It offered a chance to have direct conversations with industry experts, compare alternatives and gain practical insights into the often complex journey of building or owning a home. The lively interactions and steady patronage kept the fair buzzing throughout the day, with exhibitors attending to visitors and offering advice on how to turn their housing aspirations into reality. The three-day fair, which opened on Friday, August 21, is being held under the theme “ Dream it. Explore it. Own it .” It brings together businesses and professionals from across the housing and construction value chain, creating a platform where visitors can access a wide range of products, services and expertise under one roof. With Day Two now in the books, attention turns to the final day of the fair on Sunday, August 23, when more patrons are expected to make their way to the Achimota Retail Centre. For those still dreaming of owning a home, the message remains simple: dream it, explore it, and take the next step towards owning it. The mini-fair is being organised in partnership with Republic Bank, under its brand promise “We’re the one for you!”, and powered by Drive EV GH, which promotes sustainable mobility. Other partners supporting the initiative are Virtual Security Africa, Akwaaba Building Materials, Lesh Fortune Ltd, MTN, Door Masters, Ayuda, Western Vilas, CTECHI Ghana LTD, Saint-Gobain Ghana, Sintex Tank, Interplast and Clifton Homes.

items.title: Pêche : les acteurs du secteur plaident pour un meilleur encadrement des accords
items.description: Une table ronde consacrée au dialogue sur la politique de pêche au Sénégal s’est clôturée, hier, à Saly. Ce séminaire, organisé par la Fondation Konrad Adenauer, a été l’occasion pour les acteurs du secteur de la pêche d’échanger autour des accords de pêche avec l’Union européenne, des licences et des difficultés rencontrées par les acteurs de la pêche artisanale et industrielle. Une rencontre a réuni, du 19 au 21 août, plusieurs acteurs du secteur de la pêche à Saly. Cette initiative de la Fondation Konrad Adenauer a permis aux responsables du secteur d’échanger sur la situation de la pêche au Sénégal, les difficultés rencontrées par les professionnels et les relations du Sénégal avec l’Union européenne. Pour le représentant du président du Haut Conseil du dialogue social, Alpha Youm, la tenue de cette rencontre permet aux différents acteurs de disposer du même niveau d’information sur le secteur. « Nous sommes très satisfaits d’être ici parce qu’on a un cadre qui nous permet d’avoir une visibilité sur le secteur de la pêche, d’identifier les problèmes et les difficultés que rencontrent la pêche artisanale et la pêche industrielle, ainsi que le partenariat », a-t-il déclaré. Selon ce dernier, la pêche est un secteur « porteur de croissance et créateur d’emplois» qui doit être restructuré. «Parmi les principales recommandations, il y a le renforcement des moyens consacrés à la sécurité maritime et la poursuite du dialogue entre les acteurs de la pêche artisanale et ceux de la pêche industrielle. C’est une obligation pour restructurer le secteur», a déclaré Alpha Youm, tout en appelant à revoir et à « améliorer le partenariat entre le Sénégal et l’Union européenne, dans l’intérêt du pays ». Les conditions pour de nouveaux accords Pour sa part, Massal Fall, vétérinaire biologiste de la pêche et enseignant-chercheur au département Pêche et Aquaculture et Conservation des ressources, considère que les accords de pêche entre le Sénégal et l’Union européenne ont considérablement évolué. « Les accords de pêche ont connu plusieurs évolutions au fil des années, notamment en ce qui concerne les conditions d’accès aux ressources et leur encadrement », a-t-il expliqué. De ce fait, le chercheur estime que la question du surplus de production est importante dans la conclusion d’un accord de pêche. Dans ce sillage, l’accord entre l’UE et le Sénégal n’est plus avantageux pour l’État sénégalais, pense-t-il. « On ne peut négocier des accords que quand on a des surplus de production. Quand vous n’avez plus ce surplus de production, vous ne pouvez pas signer des accords de pêche », a-t-il soutenu. Dans ce contexte, Massal Fall estime que le Sénégal doit faire preuve de prudence dans l’octroi de nouvelles licences et la conclusion d’accords avec des partenaires étrangers. Pour lui, la priorité doit être accordée aux besoins de la population et à la préservation des ressources halieutiques.« Au-delà même de l’Union européenne, théoriquement, le Sénégal ne peut signer aucun accord avec un quelconque État tiers », a-t-il déclaré. Pour sa part, l’économiste Moustapha Dème a relevé plusieurs difficultés qui affectent le secteur, notamment la surpêche, la surcapacité de la flotte, le surinvestissement et la pêche illicite. « Aujourd’hui, il n’y a pas suffisamment de poissons pour les Sénégalais, malgré ce potentiel halieutique », a-t-il déploré. Selon lui, une partie importante des ressources débarquées est destinée aux marchés extérieurs, alors que les besoins du marché national restent importants. L’économiste déplore l’exportation de produits halieutiques en l’état , notamment les petits pélagiques congelés entiers, puis ensuite transformés dans d’autres pays. « Les femmes transformatrices auraient pu accéder à cette matière, transformer ces produits et permettre au Sénégal d’exporter des produits élaborés, transformés, qui créent de la richesse nationale, de la valeur ajoutée et consolident les emplois », a-t-il soutenu. Marième Fatou Dramé
